desc:
An account security review for SaaS apps checks how your product stores passwords, handles logins and protects each user's data, then fixes the most urgent gaps. Ecom Swift LLC delivers a plain-language report ranked by risk, with a fix beside each finding.

## What is an account security review?

An account security review is a focused inspection of everything that touches user identity in your product. We read how people sign up, log in, reset passwords, stay signed in and reach data, and we compare it against well-known good practice.

It is not a penetration test. We do not attack your live system or try to break in. We look at the design and the code, explain what is weak and show you how to repair it.

## Why accounts are where products get hurt

Accounts hold the things attackers want: personal data, payment links and the ability to act as someone else. A single weak point, such as passwords stored in a reversible form or a reset link that never expires, can expose every customer at once.

Many problems are ordinary rather than clever. A route that forgets to check who is asking, a login with no limit on guesses, or a log file that records full tokens. Small teams under deadline pressure miss these because nobody has looked at the whole picture.

## How a review improves your position

A review turns vague worry into a ranked list. Instead of "we should improve security", you get a short set of named issues, each with its risk and a suggested fix. That helps you spend limited time on what matters first.

It also helps with customers. Business buyers ask how you protect accounts, and clear answers come more easily once someone has checked. The review works by exposing gaps before an outsider does, while they are still cheap to fix. We do not promise that no incident will ever occur, and no review can.

## What a thorough review covers

- How passwords are hashed and stored.
- Login behavior, including limits on repeated guesses and lockouts.
- Reset flows, token lifetime and single use.
- Session settings: cookie flags, lifetime and sign-out behavior.
- Permission and role checks on server routes.
- Email verification and invite links.
- API keys: where they are created, shown and stored.
- Dependencies with known problems and secrets left in code or settings.
- What your logs reveal about users and requests.
- Error messages that give away more than they should.

## What we do

We begin with a short call to learn how your accounts work and which parts worry you. Then we read the relevant code and settings, and test the flows in a staging copy where possible. For each issue, we record what we found, why it matters, how serious it is and how to fix it.

The Basic package covers login, password handling, reset and sessions, with a ranked written report. Standard widens the review to permissions, rate limiting and lockouts, and applies up to five fixes in your project, followed by a re-check. Premium adds email, invite and API key review, a dependency and secrets check, up to ten fixes, a plan for the remaining items and a handover call.

You receive the findings in a form your own team can act on, plus a checklist to keep. Fixes are made in your repository so you can review each change.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Give us a staging copy so we never test on live customers.
- Fix the highest-risk items first.
- Keep a record of what changed and why.
- Re-check after fixes are applied.
- Treat the checklist as a habit, not a one-off.

**Avoid:**
- Sending production secrets or real user data.
- Assuming a login service removes every risk.
- Fixing low-risk items while serious ones wait.
- Reading the report as a certificate of safety.
- Ignoring dependency warnings because the app still runs.

## Who this is for

It suits a founder who built the login quickly and now has paying customers. It also suits a team preparing to answer a customer's security questions, or one that has had a scare and wants an outside look. A business taking over an app from another developer will find it useful as well.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of your stack and how users sign in. We need read access to the code repository as a collaborator or developer user, and a staging environment if you have one. We never need passwords, and we do not need production access. Anything we learn about your product stays between us, and the report is delivered only to you.
